notes.title: Who are the flagged wallets? Mostly retail, not bots.
notes.body: Of the 6,291 wallets flagged at p<0.01 by the orthogonality test, 62% are active retail (10–1,000 lifetime trades), 21% are sophisticated traders (high volume, diversified, 30+ day span), and only 16% are algorithmic. The insider-trading signal surfaces humans with private information far more often than it surfaces bots — the opposite of what most readers assume.

notes.title: On CNBC: bots are outperforming traders in prediction markets
notes.body: Walked through the headline finding from Paper 1 and how the dashboard makes the bot-vs-retail transfer continuously visible. Watch the full segment on CNBC.com.

notes.title: Bloomberg: 100,000 Polymarket accounts booked four-figure losses since 2025
notes.body: Bloomberg's analysis of 233M trades using the DV-PMI methodology found the typical bot averaged 89 trades per active day vs 2.2 for non-bots. Carried by Yahoo Finance, BeInCrypto, FA Magazine, Benzinga, and several wire services.

notes.title: Dashboard live at jdellavedova.com
notes.body: Public weekly release of the Della Vedova Prediction Market Indices (DV-PMI). 7 indices + per-market briefings + downloadable CSV histories, refreshed every Sunday from 671M on-chain Polymarket trades.

notes.title: Paper 2 posted to SSRN
notes.body: "Detecting Informed Trading in Prediction Markets: An Orthogonality Test" — turns the theta-epsilon orthogonality from Paper 1 into a forensic detection signal. 6,291 of 483K wallets flagged at p<0.01.
